cards.title: Find a customer using a bound PostgreSQL value
cards.explanation: Go + PostgreSQL. A caller supplies an opened pgx database pool and owns closing it. Missing ids return sql.ErrNoRows; $1 is bound by the driver.

cards.title: Read nullable contacts and close result rows
cards.explanation: Go + PostgreSQL. Nullable database fields require a nullable destination. Check iteration errors after the loop; the caller supplies the database connection.

cards.title: Transfer an order allocation with transaction rollback
cards.explanation: Go 1.23+ / pgx 5.7.6 / PostgreSQL 18.4. The caller owns the pool. Deferred rollback cleans up early errors; Commit keeps both changes. The orders fixture enforces non-negative totals. A missing row rejects the transfer instead of silently losing an allocation.

referenceTopics.title: database/sql with PostgreSQL
referenceTopics.summary: database/sql needs a driver. The playground pins pgx/v5 v5.7.6 and uses PostgreSQL $1 placeholders.
rules: database/sql needs a driver. The playground pins pgx/v5 v5.7.6 and uses PostgreSQL $1 placeholders.
Pass bound values separately. Scan can return sql.ErrNoRows; QueryContext callers must close rows and check rows.Err(). Use sql.NullString for nullable text.
Keep one transaction on one connection; check affected-row counts, roll back on any error and let the owning caller close or release the connection. Do not nest BEGIN operations.

cards.title: Query a PostgreSQL customer by id
cards.explanation: Node + PostgreSQL, pg 8.23.1. The caller supplies a connected Client and closes it in finally. The values array keeps user input separate from SQL syntax; the row type describes the expected projection.

cards.title: Commit a PostgreSQL change or roll it back
cards.explanation: Node + PostgreSQL. A duplicate key triggers rollback and restores a usable connection. A dedicated Client is required; never interleave unrelated work on this transaction connection.

cards.title: Move an order allocation atomically with pg
cards.explanation: pg 8.23.1 / TypeScript 5.9.3 / PostgreSQL 18.4. Supply an idle connected Client dedicated to this operation; do not nest inside another transaction or use pool.query. The caller closes/releases it. Both bound updates succeed or rollback together; rowCount rejects missing endpoints.

referenceTopics.title: Node PostgreSQL with pg
referenceTopics.summary: node-postgres binds $1, $2 values through a separate values array. Identifiers cannot be bound as values.
rules: node-postgres binds $1, $2 values through a separate values array. Identifiers cannot be bound as values.
Use one connected Client for an entire transaction; always roll back on failure and close/release connections in the owning caller.
Keep one transaction on one connection; check affected-row counts, roll back on any error and let the owning caller close or release the connection. Do not nest BEGIN operations.

cards.title: Find a customer with a SQLite bound parameter
cards.explanation: Python + SQLite. The trailing comma creates a one-element tuple. The caller owns the connection and closes it explicitly. Missing customers return None.

cards.title: Look up a SQLite customer by a bound name
cards.explanation: Python + SQLite. Dictionary keys omit the colon; an input containing quotes remains a value. Host-language content activates only when Python support is available.

cards.title: Import a batch atomically and keep connection ownership explicit
cards.explanation: Python 3.13 sqlite3, legacy transaction control (the sqlite3.connect default). Supply an idle connection with autocommit left at its default, not autocommit=True. A connection context commits or rolls back the entire batch but never closes it; the caller closes it explicitly. Empty batches are harmless; duplicate keys reject every insert in that batch.

referenceTopics.title: Python sqlite3 parameter binding
referenceTopics.summary: Python 3.13 sqlite3 is part of the standard library. Use ? with a tuple or :name with a dictionary.
referenceTopics.syntax:
import sqlite3
# Connection.execute(sql, parameters) binds ? sequences or :name dictionaries.
# A connection context manages commit/rollback but does not close the connection.
rules: Python 3.13 sqlite3 is part of the standard library. Use ? with a tuple or :name with a dictionary.
Close connections explicitly. A with-connection block commits or rolls back; it does not close. Enable PRAGMA foreign_keys before a transaction.

In legacy transaction control, an idle connection context rolls back a failed executemany batch; it does not close the connection. Reject an already-active transaction before starting an independently owned batch.
